top_choice_rationale: P001 pairs two achievements in which a designed molecular recognition event created a capability that did not exist: base editing (an evolved deaminase delivered by a nickase-guided protein converts a defined base without a double-strand break, a different mechanism from the 2020 prize) and heterobifunctional targeted protein degradation (2001 concept, ternary-complex energetics since quantified). Both are replicated widely, generative, and explainable in a sentence, and the allocation of Liu, Crews and Deshaies fits the three-person limit. Its weaknesses are real: Liu alone omits Komor and Gaudelli, whose papers are decisive, and no PROTAC is yet approved. That is why P002, base editing credited to Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, is my second choice. P003 follows because C-N coupling is mature and cleanly attributed but reads as an extension of the 2010 prize. P004 is next because the dye-sensitized cell is mature but has been displaced in practice. An award is still preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no credited name is at Lund University or a known collaborator. Lund colleagues Somfai and Sparr are on the committee, which is not a conflict for any proposal.
